prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] EN · Dependency audit (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Package" · longest unbreakable word 147px · one-line width 391px
  col 2: header "Version" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 91px
  col 3: header "License" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 77px
  col 4: header "Vulnerabilities" · longest unbreakable word 103px · one-line width 103px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 252px · one-line width 468px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Audit English-language dependencies for their versions, licenses, vulnerabilities, and relevant notes.","reading":"Readers scan package names to find a dependency, then read across its row; they may also compare licenses and vulnerabilities down their columns.","groups":["Package and Version identify the dependency and the release being audited.","License and Vulnerabilities are compact audit fields that readers may compare across packages.","Notes provide explanatory context for the same row and may need more reading space."],"keep_intact":["Package identifiers, especially scoped names","Version numbers","License identifiers and vulnerability values where possible","The Vulnerabilities header where possible"],"may_wrap":["Notes at natural word boundaries","Long package names at natural separator boundaries where possible","Explanatory text in other cells"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[105,49,55,75,75],"idea":"Fit all five columns in the viewport for immediate row-by-row comparison, accepting splits in identifiers, headers, and notes."},{"name":"B","widths":[168,75,98,124,150],"idea":"Preserve package identifiers and the compact audit fields while giving notes a moderate width, with horizontal scrolling to reach the later columns."},{"name":"C","widths":[168,112,98,124,273],"idea":"Favor intact identifiers and more natural note wrapping, accepting substantial horizontal scrolling across the wider table."}]}
